We introduced an AI component that detects people on the camera's videos and only triggers the alarm when the movement is really caused by a human getting close to the fence. Read More Fly-Fut Soccer Highlight Generation A company that records soccer matches with drones hired us to develop a computer vision model to pre-identify the events of a match so that editors didn't have to watch the entire game. Developing an AI pipeline that detects game objects like players, goals and ball and learns how do they interact with each other in key game events like goals, shots and penalties, we reduced five times the amount of time it takes to edit a match. More Details Crezer SA CCTV Human Movement Detection Some of our client security cameras were having trouble with intruder alarms that were actually triggered by wild animals getting close to the fence. Built-in cameras movement detectors were alarming when anything moved, and 99% of the time it was a false alarm. We introduced an AI component that detects people on the camera's videos and only triggers the alarm when the movement is really caused by a human getting close to the fence. The false alarms dropped by 80%, while maintaining a 80% recall on human detection on a series of data where we analyzed the impact of our solution. More Details ELDES Sign Language Detection EldeS is a project created in order to support and popularize the use of Sign Language by integrating technology into teaching and achieving a greater inclusion of people with hearing impairment. As a first MVP of how Computer Vision can be used to help Sign Language teaching, we developed a web-based app that detects when the user correctly does a gesture to represent numbers 1 to 10 and letters V and Y. We used MediaPipe Hand Detection model, and code our own logic on how to recognize these gestures based on hand keypoint detection. We turned EldeS ideas into an MVP that helped them to access investment and start the development of the final product, a path we are currently walking together now. More Details Teaching computers to see When training Computer Vision models, we are actually making computers capable of seeing and understanding the outside world. Movement Analysis The human body is a complex machine capable of countless movements and poses. Using body keypoint detectors like OpenPose or BlazePose, we write custom logic to detect when the user starts or stops a specific movement, for example, a Yoga Asana or a Crossfit series workout.
